title: The Shunemite, Oppressed with Grief
description: The Shunemite, Oppressed with Grief in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 13, “The Shunemite. 2Ki 4:31”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Shu-ne-mite, op-pressed with grief, When she had lost the son she loved, Went to El-i-sha for re-lief, Nor vain her ap-pli-ca-tion proved.

lines: The Shunemite, oppressed with grief,
When she had lost the son she loved,
Went to Elisha for relief,
Nor vain her application proved.
He sent his servant on before
To lay a staff upon his head;
This he could do, but do no more,
He left him, as he found him, dead.
But when the Lord'S almighty pow'r
Wrought with the prophet's prayer, and faith,
The mother saw a joyful hour,
She saw her child restored from death.
Thus, like the weeping Shunemite,
For many, dead in sin we grieve;
Now, Lord, display thine arm of might,
Cause them to hear thy voice and live.
Thy preachers bear the staff in vain,
Though at thine own command we go;
Lord, we have tried, and tried again,
We find them dead, and leave them so.
Come then thyself--to every heart
The glory of thy name make known;
The means are our appointed part,
The pow'r and grace are thine alone.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
